children: Kuwait has approved the reallocation of a 2.5 million square metre (sqm) site in Al-Zour to Kuwait Gulf Oil Company (KGOC) to support the expansion of onshore processing facilities for the offshore Dorra field, local Arabic language newspaper Alanba reported on Wednesday.

The committee approved a request to cancel the site's allocation for the Third Olefins and Second Aromatics Project (D2) and reallocate the land to KGOC for the expansion of the Dorra field's onshore processing project, facilities and installations (OPF), the report said.
It said the decision was taken after obtaining approvals from the relevant authorities, including Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC), Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) and the Ministry of Oil.

The Dorra gas field, estimated to contain reserves of around 20 trillion cubic feet, lies in the offshore Partitioned Neutral Zone (PNZ) shared by Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. It is managed by Al-Khafji Joint Operations (KJO), a joint venture between KGOC and Aramco Gulf Operations Company.

Last month, a report by The Times Kuwait online news outlet, citing Dubai-based project intelligence portal MEED, said KJO awarded four engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) packages – three offshore and one onshore – for the development of Dorra field with a combined value of nearly $7 billion.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Kuwait reallocates 2.5mln sqm Al-Zour site for Dorra field processing facilities
